scope: Single native promoter per checkout and atomic canonical-file publication; process interruption and CLI error visibility
head: 01cea8deda48d84b6a2993cd4bdefe8280082c0b
counterproofs: File fsync or os.replace failure preserves previous canonical bytes and source proposal; staged file cleaned on ordinary exception
Two actual forked processes contend for directory flock: second fails PROMOTION_BUSY while first holds lock, first publishes once
Actual SIGKILL before os.replace keeps previous canonical file and proposal; OS releases lock, native retry succeeds
Interrupted temporary .tmp is never treated as canonical Markdown; no automatic purge of remnants
Parent directory fsync failure after publication reports explicit partial effect and preserves proposal
CLI apply failure returns exit 1 and visible details in text and JSON, instead of false success
decisions: Use native POSIX flock on checkout directory inode; no lockfile registry or new scheduler
Same-directory temporary file, flush/fsync, final freshness check, os.replace and directory fsync
Only cooperating native promoters are mutually excluded. Existing approved-target guard retained.
limits: Directory flock is advisory and scoped to this checkout, not a distributed lock across worktrees or uncooperative authors.
Proposal authors that bypass the lock can still change source between comparison and unlink; no universal atomic transaction across proposal and canonical files.
SIGKILL before replacement was tested, not machine power loss or crash at every syscall. A .tmp orphan may remain; it is ignored as content and not silently purged.
A crash or fsync error after publication can leave canonical file published and source retained; no two-file rollback or automatic recovery journal claimed.
Complete withdrawal trigger is still undefined in native policy; user clarification requested. No inferred withdrawal, newly accepted contract, executable removal connection or indexed-page deletion.
No corpus/shared DB write, runtime activation, CI, commit/push/merge or deployment.
